items.title: Exercise1.7: genuine square-root perturbation energy (supporting step)

source.attribution: Sinho Chewi's exercise; original ASTIS elaboration of its omitted energy calculation, not a source quotation or complete exercise answer.

items.statement: The LSI-to-PI route requires the actual square-root affine perturbation's finite derivative energy and its quadratic coefficient. For a differentiable bounded real test with integrable squared derivative norm, small real parameters give actual integrable square-root derivative energy, and its punctured normalized integral tends to one quarter of the original energy. This generic analytic supporting result does not identify a canonical RN Fisher functional or establish LSI admissibility.
assumptions: The source consumer uses smooth bounded compact-gradient tests under a probability law. Its original gradient-energy integrability and global test conditions still require proof.

The generic intermediate theorem assumes genuine differentiability, a finite a.e. bound and integrable actual squared derivative norm. The measurable topology makes continuous real functions measurable; no finite-measure, centering or probability hypothesis is required.
The eventual actual-energy integrability conclusion includes zero; the quotient limit is explicitly punctured and two-sided.

obligations.label: Genuine derivative and derived small-parameter measurability, domination and energy integrability
Actual dominated quadratic limit with exact coefficient1/4
Derive source-test energy assumptions, noncompact LSI admissibility, entropy/cutoff extension and final PI/core closure

bindings.boundary: Only a generic explicit differentiable-function energy result. Original energy integrability remains an input here and must be derived in the final exercise; canonical Fisher, LSI/PI, full exercise and Bench admission remain separate.

assumption_deltas.source: Euclidean smooth bounded compact-gradient tests under the source probability law.
assumption_deltas.lean: A real normed measurable space with open sets measurable, an arbitrary measure, genuine differentiability, an a.e. bound and integrable original squared derivative norm.
assumption_deltas.reason: This is an intermediate analytic lemma, not the final exercise. No finite-measure, probability or centering assumption is used. The exercise must still derive its genuine source-test energy integrability; it cannot silently acquire that as a new public premise.

assumption_deltas.source: Euclidean gradient-energy calculation used after an actual LSI-domain justification.
assumption_deltas.lean: Squared operator norm of the actual Frechet derivative of the explicit square-root function; the focused test proves its Hilbert gradient form by Riesz isometry.
assumption_deltas.reason: No RN a.e. substitution is differentiated, and a.e. positivity is not global smoothness or LSI admissibility. These domains remain separate obligations.
